results: 1. Neurological examination focusing on cerebellar signs (finger-to-nose, heel-to-shin, dysdiadochokinesia, tandem gait, Romberg test)
Romberg test: negative - swaying is not worse with the eyes closed
coordination examination (limb and truncal): limb and truncal ataxia
2. MRI of the brain with attention to the cerebellum and brainstem
brain MRI: cerebellar atrophy at one year; serial imaging over five years shows progressive ISOLATED cerebellar atrophy with no supratentorial abnormality
3. Genetic testing for Friedreich's ataxia (GAA trinucleotide repeat expansion)
genetic ataxia panel: no pathogenic repeat expansion or variant
copper / caeruloplasmin: normal - excludes Wilson disease
7. Complete blood count and comprehensive metabolic panel
serum electrolytes, urea and creatinine: normal
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Spinocerebellar ataxia (hereditary isolated cerebellar ataxia) with primary Purkinje cell degeneration — genetically unclassified, likely a rare autosomal dominant SCA subtype (e.g., SCA 5, SCA 31, or other locus) given progressive isolated cerebellar atrophy with normal peripheral nerves and negative standard genetic panel

Alternatives:
1. Expansive repeat disorder not detected on standard panel (e.g., somatic instability reducing blood-based detection in late-onset SCA 6 or SCA 31)
2. Autosomal recessive cerebellar ataxia due to novel or unsequenced gene variant (ARCA not captured by standard panel)
3. GLUT1 deficiency syndrome or other metabolic cerebellar degeneration with late/progressive presentation
